question: In Fresenius SE & Co. KGaA's press release for Q4 and FY 2025 (dated February 25, 2026), was Group free cash flow higher in full-year 2025 than in full-year 2024, and what does the release say this free cash flow figure is measured after? Also, how did Q4/25 compare with Q4/24?
reference_answer: No. Group free cash flow was €1,285 million in FY 2025 versus €1,679 million in FY 2024, a decline of 23%. In Q4/25 it was higher: €966 million versus €580 million in Q4/24 (+67%). According to the release's footnote, this free cash flow is 'after acquisitions, dividends and lease liabilities' (continuing operations), and the release also notes that prior-year figures were adjusted due to the gradual exit from Fresenius Vamed.

question: In Fresenius' Q4/FY 2025 press release, what was the Group's net debt/EBITDA ratio at the end of 2025 versus 2024, what target corridor does the release compare it to, and on what basis does the release say the ratio is calculated?
reference_answer: The net debt/EBITDA ratio was 2.7x at year-end 2025 versus 3.0x in 2024 (the release describes this as an improvement of 30 bp), 'well within the self-imposed target corridor of 2.5 to 3.0x'. The release's footnote defines the basis: at average exchange rates for both net debt and EBITDA; pro forma closed acquisitions/divestitures, including lease liabilities, including the Fresenius Medical Care dividend, and net debt adjusted for the valuation effect of the exchangeable bond.

question: What full-year 2026 guidance for the Fresenius Group does the Q4/FY 2025 press release give (organic revenue growth, constant currency Core EPS growth and EBIT margin), what 2025 base figures does it attach to the revenue and Core EPS guidance, and is the EBIT margin figure part of the official guidance?
reference_answer: For FY 2026 the release guides Fresenius Group organic revenue growth of 4% to 7% (2025 revenue base: €22,554 million) and constant currency Core EPS growth of 5% to 10% (2025 Core EPS base: €2.87; Core EPS is before special items and excludes Fresenius Medical Care). It also shows an EBIT margin of ~11.5% (2025 base: €2,595 million EBIT), but this is not part of the official guidance: the release states it is provided solely for modelling purposes.

question: Belfius' 2025 annual results press release (consolidated, 31 December 2025) and the Belfius Bank 2025 Pillar 3 report both quote the CET1 ratio and total risk exposure amount (TREA). What CET1 ratio and TREA does each document give for end-2025, and, on each document's own comparison basis for end-2024, did TREA decrease or increase during 2025?
reference_answer: The press release gives a CET1 ratio of 15.9% and a total risk exposure of €72.1 billion at end-2025, compared with €75.2 billion at end-2024 (as originally reported under CRR2), i.e. a decrease, which it attributes to the entry into force of CRR3. The Pillar 3 report gives the same figures with more precision: CET1 15.87% and TREA of EUR 72.148 billion, but compares with EUR 71.533 billion at end-2024 on a pro forma CRR 3 basis, i.e. an increase of EUR 615 million. The apparent contradiction is a basis difference (published CRR2 vs pro forma CRR3 for 2024); the press release figures are rounded and unaudited.

evidence.text: The CET1 ratio stands at 15.9%, up slightly from 2024, mainly due to a decrease in total risk exposure to €72.1 billion (compared to €75.2 billion at the end of 2024), due to the entry into force of CRR3
At the end of 2025, the CET 1 capital ratio amounted to 15.87%, a decrease of 29 bps
At the end of December 2025, Belfius TREA amounted to EUR 72.148 billion, an increase … by EUR +615 million compared to EUR 71.533 billion at the end of 2024 (proforma CRR 3).

question: Fresenius Group's EBIT for fiscal year 2025 is €2,595 million in the Q4/FY 2025 press release but €2,310 million in the consolidated segment reporting of the 2025 annual report. How large is the difference, and what explains it according to the two documents' basis labels (before vs after special items by segment)?
reference_answer: The difference is €285 million (€2,595 million minus €2,310 million). The press release reports Group EBIT before special items (Fresenius Kabi €1,413 million, Fresenius Helios €1,328 million, Group Corporate -€146 million). In the annual report's segment reporting, Kabi (€1,413 million) and Helios (€1,328 million) are also before special items, but Corporate / Other (-€431 million) is after special items, so the Group column of €2,310 million is not purely before special items. The €285 million gap equals the difference between Corporate -€146 million (release) and Corporate / Other -€431 million (annual report).

question: Recompute Belfius' consolidated cost-to-income ratio for 2025 by dividing the management report's COSTS line by its INCOME line (both in € million). Does the result, rounded to one decimal place, match the 43.0% cost-income ratio that the press release reports?
reference_answer: Yes. COSTS of €1,845 million divided by INCOME of €4,295 million gives 42.96%, i.e. 43.0% to one decimal place, which matches the reported cost-income ratio of 43.0% at 31.12.2025 (43.2% at 31.12.2024).
